answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then slash it when a blinded audit finds fabricated work or coordinated duplicate claims. Audits sample tasks and compare independently verifiable outputs, so a velvet profile or falcon badge earns no trust by itself; the cost is capital locked per identity and forfeited when caught. Spreading a campaign across many accounts multiplies that exposure, while a comet-like burst of signups can trigger more audits, making cheap identity creation costly rather than impossible.
